utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Docherty, you are to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Good morning again, Mr. Katic. I trust you had a pleasant weekend. Mr. Katic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please speak up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, when we broke Friday, we were going through Prosecution exhibit 496.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I would ask that to be brought back to the screen. I have just a couple of more questions about that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you see it there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I'd like to direct your attention to paragraph number 3, down at the bottom of -- down towards the bottom of the screen. I'm going to read it in English. I'd just ask to you listen and make sure I read it correctly: "I forbid all use of weapons of bigger calibre on civilian targets in Sarajevo without my approval." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are again facing the same problem like the last time. That the witness is asked to interpret the contents of a document and I object to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We haven't heard a question yet, Mr. Tapuskovic, and last time I ruled that he wasn't being asked to do what you said. You said then he was being asked to interpret the intentions of Mr. Mladic, and at that time my determination was that that was not the case. But your strike is preemptive. Let us see what the question and then we will see where we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So, Mr. Katic, this paragraph number 3 does not then forbid the use of smaller calibre against targets in Sarajevo, does it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, looking and considering carefully paragraph 3, and if it is -- if I'm to speak as a psychologist, that would seem to be the case, based on this language. However, it is inconceivable to me that this sentence can be interpreted that we are not going to use heavy weaponry, but we are going to fire from infantry weapons. I really am reluctant to comment on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I understand your reluctance, Mr. Katic, but all I'm asking you is what the plain language of the document says. And if I understood your answer correctly, you say that it does seem to allow the use of smaller calibre weapons against civilian targets, but that you cannot really believe that it says that. Is that a fair summary of what you just told the Court?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to shift to -- I'm staying on this document but a rightly different topic. If I understood your direct examination by Mr. Tapuskovic correctly, you indicated that had you some question as to whether this meeting had taken place, and this was when you were testifying that General Mladic may have been misunderstood. Did I understand correctly that you expressed some doubt as to whether there meeting in Vogosca on the 5th of November had ever occurred, or did I misunderstand?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this meeting in that form, so to say, involving all the civilians representatives of the Serbian Sarajevo, apart from me, didn't take place, and I think that you understand from my statement before the lawyer what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Actually, I was basing my question upon what you said to the lawyers in your statement back in August, when you spoke with Mr. Hogan and Mr. Sachdeva from the Office of the Prosecutor, rather than denying that such a meeting had occurred, you speculated a bit about who might have been in attendance. Do you recall that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I do remember a conversation in August with the investigators in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And did you, during that conversation in Sarajevo, with the investigators in August of 2006, talk about who might have been present at this meeting in Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that had that meeting happened, Mr. Stanisic might have been present, the president of Vogosca municipality, Mr. Koprivica; vice-president of the town of the Serbian Sarajevo, Mr. Radic. In other words, I said that these persons who were working in Vogosca might have been there if the meeting indeed had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You testified on Friday, when we just began a little bit of cross-examination, that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps had communications equipment, radios, and field telephones, and you talked about stringing the wires for the telephone. Isn't the case, sir, that General Mladic could have communicated with General Milosevic and learned immediately from him about what had happened in Vogosca on the 5th of November?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, all these questions involve assumptions. The witness said decidedly that he never attended that meeting, and he keeps using the word "if." I don't know why we are now in the area of suppositions, although the witness said that he has no knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I think the last question is improper and invites speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let me ask the question this way. On Friday, you testified that the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps had field telephones and radios, is that correct, and that you knew this from your time as a serving soldier in 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: During your -- excuse me. This document in paragraph number 1 mentions UNPROFOR; and during your examination-in-chief, you testified about relations with UNPROFOR, and in particular, I believe, you mentioned several times the good relations that you had with the G5 of the French Battalion. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could please see 65 ter number 03147.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, on the right-hand side is the B/C/S version of this document and on the left is the English. Is this a communication from Sarajevo-Romanija Corps command, and is it dated 26th November 1994?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time that I see this document. I can see in the letterhead, "The Command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps." I have read the document itself, and I can see that someone else has signed it on behalf of the commander, and I don't know whose signature this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The question I actually asked, sir, was whether it was dated the 26th of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says here the date, 26th November, and that's in the letterhead.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And this is dated -- by being dated 26th of November, this is approximately 21 days, if my arithmetic is right, after the order from General Mladic, is that correct, three weeks, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is true that between the 5th and the 26th, the period is 21 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And now let's get to the signature. In the lower left-hand side, it says, "Komandant, General Major Dragomir Milosevic," correct, and then there is a stamp with Cyrillic lettering on it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in the centre of the stamp, the Serbian double-headed eagle; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the last line of this document says: "You are to fire at the centre of deployed UNPROFOR forces," doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to switch topics now, sir. Do you recall testifying concerning the confrontation lines on Debelo Brdo, a hill to the south of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I said that there was a conflict surrounding Debelo Brdo; however, as far as I know, not exactly to the south, if that is the same hill where I was deployed as a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I think we're talking about the same hill; and if we're not, I think it will become clear in a moment or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Before I go on, Mr. President, could I please tender the document that is now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P751, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You are from Sarajevo, Mr. Katic, and have lived there all your life. Am I right about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: As a result, you know the city well, and the area around the city, also, you know that well?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I know it pretty well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And as you've testified a couple of times, as a private soldier serving in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, you were stationed at the base of Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wasn't Debelo Brdo, and I wasn't on Debelo Brdo as a soldier ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Then I perhaps misunderstood. Where were you -- where was your station when you were a soldier in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the line between Vrace, or rather, my house in Ohridska Street, towards Zlatiste, and that is as far as Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I see. Okay. Thank you for the clarification. Are you then familiar with the confrontation lines in the area of Debelo Brdo, about which you testified after all, on direct examination?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And so you are aware that the United Nations actually had an observation post on the very, very top of Debelo Brdo, and then below them was the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that on the peak of Debelo Brdo were members of UNPROFOR; and almost at the same elevation, but on the other side, were members of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then below the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was the army of Republika Srpska, the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps specifically; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Where, then, was the army of Republika Srpska? On Debelo Brdo itself.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no VRS troops on Debelo Brdo itself. They were on the line towards Zlatiste, if one climbs towards Mount Trebevic on the right-hand side starting from Grbavica. If you can understand what an I'm saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I think in a minute we'll see a photograph that will help us; but in any event, of the two warring factions, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina did have the high ground on the hill called Debelo Brdo itself; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. But to the south of Debelo Brdo, there is a ridge line, is that correct, more hills?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lower hills to the south are below Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Aren't those hills in fact higher than Debelo Brdo? From the hills to the south, do you not look down on the top of Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they are not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could we please see a photograph with 65 ter number 03185.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, as someone who has lived in Sarajevo all his life, do you recognise the scene that's in the photograph on the monitor in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you see that in the centre of the photograph, a little bit to the viewers right, there is the peak of a lower hill than the one on which the photographer is standing. That lower peak, sir, is Debelo Brdo, is it not?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph is made very well, and it is true that this thing down there is the peak of Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And behind Debelo Brdo, you can see the city of Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And this photograph was taken from the south, looking to the north; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And this photograph is taken from territory that during the armed conflict was under the command of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably from the distance where the Republika Srpska army troops were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll tender this photograph into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P752, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And at this point, Mr. President, I'll call for Prosecution Exhibit 194. It is a map. It will take a while to load, and I will continue my examination while that is going on. Judge Harhoff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: While we wait for the next exhibit, my question to the witness is whether the building that we can see on top of Debelo Brdo is the observe post?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the UNPROFOR observation post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, while we wait for the map, there was testimony earlier in this trial from a Canadian army general named David Fraser, and I'm going to tell you some of the things he testified to and ask whether you agree or disagree. At one point in his testimony, he was asked to describe an imaginary walk from the top of Debelo Brdo to the south, and he said: "Well, if you went south, you actually walked down a bit of a hill but then uphill, where in fact the Serbs had their positions which was slightly above Debelo Brdo, and you could leaning over the sort of a little bit of a dip in the flat area and up higher, and that's where the Serbs were, all along the ridge line." Is that a fair characterisation of the situation around Debelo Brdo, Mr. Katic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is it partially true that the land to the south of Debelo Brdo is in fact above Debelo Brdo, as we saw in the photograph we just admitted into evidence, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Zlatiste, the Republika Srpska army had its positions; and until June, this was the territory controlled by the Bosnia-Herzegovina army. This was the communication route, a road leading to the Mount Trebevic and Pale from Grbavica and Lukavica. In relation to Debelo Brdo, this elevation is deep inside a wooded area; and from the woods, it's a pine wood, you can see the top of Debelo Brdo, the UNPROFOR observation post, and all the way down to what this gentleman from the Canadian battalion just mentioned; and then all the way down to Strma Stijena, the sheer cliffs, that's where the Republika Srpska had its positions. And in relation to Debelo Brdo, it is not high ground, subsequently speaking. But below Debelo Brdo, heading towards Kovacici and Grbavica, wherever the troops were stationed along the separation lines, the Debelo Brdo elevation was the high ground in relation to all those positions in the direction of the separation line at Kovacici and then further on to Vrbanja bridge and Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: If we could turn then to the map, I'll ask the usher to zoom in on the area south and very slightly east of the city, which is the area of Debelo Brdo that we've been discussing.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, just take a moment and get oriented with that map. Let me know when you are oriented, and then I will have one or two questions for you. Mr. Katic, would it help if we zoomed in a bit, or is this good for you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to zoom it in a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sure. How's that, better?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It's better now, but I can't read any of the letters. But I will, I hope, manage to find my way around it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, if you can't, that's all right. There's other evidence, but I did want to ask you this: This is the map that during his testimony the Canadian officer used to talk about the confrontation lines and the area of town that you have been giving your testimony about. And so my question would be: Can you confirm that these confrontation lines, red for the army of Republika Srpska and blue for the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, are accurate as shown on this map?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it's 95 per cent accurate, the separation lines, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: When you say it's 95 per cent accurate, does that mean it's, in a general sense, accurate; or does that mean that you've actually seen some specific inaccuracy, and that's the 5 per cent that's not accurate?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that it is possible to orient oneself well on this map. I don't know whether the separation lines as drawn here on the right-hand side are completely accurate. Here it's possible to see; and, in fact, based on what you asked me, the Zlatiste-Debelo Brdo separation line is the point, and I don't know if that's what I can see here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, let's -- let's move on then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I'll ask now for another photograph. It's 65 ter number 03186.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, again, Mr. Katic, as a life-long resident of the city of Sarajevo, do you recognise the scene that's depicted in the photograph now in front of you on the monitor?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that this is taken from a spot on the road that runs between Lukavica and Pale along the ridge line to the south of the city of Sarajevo. Is that an accurate description?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been taken from one stretch of the road, either from the road itself or maybe a little bit further down from the road. It's impossible for me to determine on the basis of this photograph whether this was taken from the territory held by the Republika Srpska army or the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. But even if it had been taken from the part of the road from Zlatiste to Mount Trebevic, about 100 metres down that road, you could actually see this from that road, from that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. If the hill called Debelo Brdo would be just off to the left margin of this photograph, not entirely in the photograph; but, in other words, the one that we looked at a few minutes ago, if the photographer turned a little to the right, this would be the seen that would be visible. Am I right about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the left of this photograph, there's Debelo Brdo. It may be about 300 metres away from the location where this photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the top of Debelo Brdo, again, would be below the level at which this photograph was taken; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a surveyor, and I can't determine the -- whether the actual height of Debelo Brdo is level with this or whether one has -- is on the high ground in relation to the other. On the basis of actually looking at this location where this photograph may have been taken from, in my opinion, they -- those two sites may have been level, so this position here and the summit of Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Katic, that the witness before you was an operations officer, a major, in the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what position he held in that corps. I saw the gentleman here, but I don't know what post he held in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, the reason that I'm asking the question is because in your last answer you expressed some doubt as to which army controlled the land on which this photograph was taken, and I wanted to, for the record, point out that on page --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, page 5498 of the transcript at lines 15 through 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- when shown a photograph, either this photograph on one like it said that "from the elevation controlled by the SRK, there is a much better view, 50 per cent better. It is in our territory way up above the road." Is there even higher ground behind the photograph? I'm not asking to you be is surveyor. I'm asking you as a life-long resident of the city of Sarajevo who knows the city well. In other words, if one turned 180 degrees from this photograph and started walking, once you crossed the road, you would start climbing, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. But what you're asking me is what I'm telling you. This photograph may have been taken both from the territory held by the Bosnia-Herzegovina army. I know that the road to Mount Trebevic very well, but I don't see that it looks even close to that, and the separation lines went along the road to Mount Trebevic. I have to answer that behind the road, or if I take a 180 degree turn, I can see the mountains are ever higher. Those are the slopes of Mount Trebevic which are quite high. So if you look -- if you turn around by 180 degrees, and if you look in that direction from the road, you will see those -- the high mountain; that is Mount Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And my question to you, sir, was: Wasn't the witness, the Defence witness who preceded you, correct when he said that that even-- whoever controlled this ground, that that even higher ground, what you call the slopes of Mount Trebevic, was controlled by the SRK; and, as the preceding witness said, it's our territory, way up above the road, and that's where the view was not a bit better but considerably better. And those are direct quotations from his testimony. Wasn't he right in what he testified to, Mr. Katic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're now quoting to me what the previous witness had said, and I said that if you turn by 180 degrees from the site where this photograph was taken, there is higher ground ahead. And probably if you were to climb up to much higher ground than where this photograph was taken, you would be able to see the city even better.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And that higher ground, from which you can see the city even better, was under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the locations from the site, and if you take this turn of 180 degrees and you go in that direction, they were held -- all these areas were held by Sarajevo-Romanija Corps of the VRS, and there were many villages there that were part of Republika Srpska. I showed you where the separation line was, and the military and the local residents who were able to move freely behind the separation lines. They were able to tend their cattle, gather hazelnuts. I really don't know why you're asking me all these question, because I don't know what the previous witness had testified.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, I tell you what, then let's forget about the previous witness. But it is your testimony that the higher ground above the road, the higher ground above the point where this photograph, was taken was under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps? Just yes or no, Mr. Katic, and then we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could I tender this photograph shall please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P753, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, during your examination-in-chief, there was some testimony about the kinds of weapons that were available to the army of Republika Srpska in the area of Grbavica. Do you remember that testimony, the questions from Mr. Tapuskovic, the answers that you gave?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I'll characterise that testimony that -- would it be fair to say that you asserted that only light infantry weapons, semi-automatic and single-shot weapons, were available in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that at Grbavica there had been no heavy weapons, only automatic and semi-automatic weapons were used, and there were three or four armoured personnel carriers and anti-aircraft guns were mounted on those vehicles, and I think that there was also a 20 millimetre gun mounted on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: A 20-millimetre gun can be used as an anti-aircraft weapon. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I said that there was an anti-aircraft gun, machine-gun mounted on those carriers, and it can be used to target aeroplanes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And anti-aircraft guns of that sort can also be lowered to fire horizontally, and they're not meant to be used that way, but they can be used against people, vehicles, and buildings; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably they can be used that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And the 20-millimetre anti-aircraft guns that have you seen, you know that they can come as a single barrel, a double barrel, or even a triple barreled weapon; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they can, yes, but that is immaterial, whether you have a one, two, or three barrels.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, regardless of whether it is material or immaterial, the answer would be yes, they do some in those different configurations. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And isn't it also true, Mr. Katic, that there were both 60-millimetre and 82 millimetre mortars in Grbavica under the control of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps throughout the time of the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no such mortars at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Isn't it also true that over and above mortars, there were tanks in Grbavica? And I'm not confusing them with armoured personnel carriers; I mean, tanks in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I became the president at Grbavica, I did not see any tanks at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Wasn't there, for example, a tank parked -- well, first of all, there is a street in Grbavica called Lenjinova Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And wasn't there, throughout much of the armed conflict, a tank parked in Lenjinova Street, which occasionally came out and fire add few rounds towards the Bosnian side?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, and I did not see this tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could we please see Prosecution Exhibit 33, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if you want to just take a moment, Mr. Katic. First of all, have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can we enlarge it a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There we are, and just before -- this is addressed to Major-General Dragomir Milosevic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Dated 8th of June, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And now if with he could scroll up past the address so that the text is fully displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, if you haven't seen it before, I'll just ask you to take a moment and read those two paragraphs to yourself, and then I'll have a question about it.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen this text before, so please give me a minute to read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And you understand that the person who wrote this letter --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And if we could, sir, just scroll down and see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: -- is an UNPROFOR sector commander, "H. Gobillard." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And did you read in the text that this is a protest of an attack all along the line, on the 8th of June, 1995, with both artillery and tanks? Did you read that part?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And in particular, do you see the -- in the first paragraph, about five or six -- about the middle of the paragraph, one tank even fired from inside Grbavica and incendiary rounds were also observed? Do you see the sentence, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do see.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you accept there were in fact tanks in Grbavica and that they were used to shell the Bosnian side of the Miljacka river, having seen this document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying this again. This is the 8th of June, 1995, when offensives started from the side of the Bosnia-Herzegovina army. At that time, as the president at Grbavica, I did not know who was shooting, how they were shooting. At that period, and this seems to be the 8th of June, everything was on fire. As they say in our language, heaven and earth was burning, but I was not aware that we had tanks at Grbavica, especially after the decision from 1994 about the grouping of heavy weaponry on certain locations outside the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Sir, the question I asked you was: Whether having seen this document, you accept that the SRK had tanks in Grbavica and that those tanks were used to fire on the Bosnian side of the Miljacka river?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And we'll get to the question of the total exclusion zone in a few minutes. You understand, Mr. Katic, that this letter was written by a Major-General within UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You understand that it was written to, addressed to major-general Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You understand that this French general would not send letters such as this to people who were unable to do something about the situation, which the French general was protesting against?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot go into such details as to whether what the French major-general is writing is true. I keep saying that I don't know and I don't believe that there was one or more tanks at Grbavica at the time. I did not leave my office at the time to see if it was a tank firing, an APC, or any other kind of weapon, or from which side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. So the answer is, if I can characterise it, that you don't accept, because you don't know. You're not denying it. Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm denying it because I don't know whether one or another weapon was fired from. If the major-general from France says that he saw it, I cannot say what he saw. I'm claiming, though, that there were no tanks in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Here's the difficulty I'm having, Mr. Katic, and maybe you can help me with it. In your direct examination, you were quite emphatic that there were no happy weapons in Grbavica. There were automatic and semi-automatic infantry weapons only. And now when shown this document, you seem to be saying that you don't know, because you were in your office all the time, and so you don't know what weapons there were in Grbavica. I see those two answers as not the same, but maybe I'm misunderstanding you; and if I am, could be help me out and clarify that, please?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you again. I saw APCs in Grbavica and I saw them in use. As far as tanks are concerned, in the period when I was in Grbavica, there were none. I didn't see any. I think I was clear. A tank, though, could have been brought, if such a possibility existed, within an hour from Lukavica, and it could have then been brought out again, but I wouldn't know that. In the time that I was at Grbavica, there were no tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And 60- and 82-millimetre mortars could also have been brought within an hour and used; and because you were in your office a lot, you wouldn't have known that either. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's correct that I didn't know that, but I claim that mortars were not brought to Grbavica to fire at Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Even though you were in your office quite a bit and, therefore, can't really say whether or not tanks were brought forward, you will still insist on denying that mortars were brought forward. Am I understanding you correctly, Mr. Katic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, Mr. Katic, that you're not really in a position to say whether there were heavy weapons or not in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said what kind of weapons existed at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I tell you what? Let move to the next topic, because I sense that we're sort of going around in a circle here. Again, you know the city of Sarajevo; and, in particular, you know Grbavica quite well, because it's the area where you lived and it's the area for which you had a certain level of political responsibility throughout the armed conflict. So you do know Grbavica, which is a municipality of the Novo Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Across the Miljacka river from Grbavica is a neighbourhood known as Marindvor; is that correct? That's where the Holiday Inn stands, the Faculty of Philosophy, the Museum of the Revolution. Do you know the area to which I'm referring?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And during your time living in Sarajevo, have you ridden the tram that goes along the street in front of the Holiday Inn?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And you know that either right in front of the Holiday Inn or a little bit to one side or the other, there is an S-curve in the tram tracks, isn't there? I'm sorry. You have to answer with words, because the court reporter can't take down a head nod. I know what you mean, but you have to say it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. When you're riding that tram, in order to negotiate that S-curve, the tram has to go pretty slowly, doesn't it, so as not to jump off the rails?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tram moved in Sarajevo at a speed of about 30 kilometres an hour; and in that section about which you are asking me, it's normal that it had to slow down because it was crossing from one side of the street to another. And, of course, if you are taking -- negotiating a bend, you have to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And just a few points about geography at the Grbavica-Marindvor area. The city of Sarajevo at that point is a bit narrower than it is at other points, and any traffic going east and west through that area would have been exposed to fire from any snipers that there might have been in Grbavica. True?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said that I didn't see snipers from either side; and specifically speaking about Grbavica, that area cannot be targeted because it's linked to the line Kovacici-Marindvor. It's lower downstream.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, we're going to talk in a few minutes about whether there were snipers in Grbavica. I know what you have testified to on that point. My question for now is simply: Traffic moving east or west through the city of Sarajevo, when it passes through the Marindvor area, and let me just be very clear, would have been exposed to sniper fire from Grbavica had there been snipers in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been exposed to fire from Kovacici, but not sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I tell you what? Let's take a look, please, at an aerial photograph, 65 ter number 02825. Do you see that in front of you, Mr. Katic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Maybe just to orient yourself, you could find the Faculty of Philosophy, the museum, and then there's a particular high-rise in Grbavica called the Metalka building; and I think if you locate those three points, we'll then be ready to proceed with some questions.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see the Faculty of Philosophy and I see the museum; and on the other side, I see Holiday Inn and the buildings in the municipality of Serbian Novo Sarajevo, but I keep telling you that this place is called Kovacici, not Grbavica. Grbavica would be to the right from the area covered by this photograph, and I have been telling you for a while that it is Kovacici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If you're going to ask questions about these three locations, maybe it's as well that he marked them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That was going to be next.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to make some marks on this photograph, so we all understand and we're all on the same page. Would you mark the Faculty of Philosophy with an F, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would you mark the museum with a M, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would you mark the Holiday Inn - excuse me - with HI, for the English "Holiday Inn."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And would you mark the Metalka building -- well, we've used M, so let's just use B for the English word "building."

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which letter?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: B, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And are you sure that you've marked the correct building for Metalka? And I'm talking about the building that's got the Metalka home appliance shop on the ground floor, from whence it gets the name Metalka.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and does the building that you've marked with a B, does that extend then to the viewer's left? In other words, have you marked the right side of the building? Right-hand side of the building, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here on the ground floor, there is a shop; and in this building here, Invest Bank was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let me make this clear. There's a shop on the ground floor of which building, the building with the B or the building to its left?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With a B.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And the Invest Bank is in the building with the B or the building to its left?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the left building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And are both the building with the B and the building to its left in territory -- well, do you see the Miljacka river in this photograph or at least the trees on either bank of the Miljacka river?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could you draw a line along the Miljacka, please.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That line that you have just drawn is also the line separating the two warring factions during the armed conflict, isn't it, with the army of Republika Srpska to the top of the photograph and the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the bottom of the photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The separation line went along the Miljacka river; in other words, of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was on this side, and the VRS with the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps on the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. And just because when you saw "this side," and "that side," it doesn't really make a good record, bear with me, I have to ask a couple of clarifying questions. When you say that the army of Republika Srpska was on this side, is that the side that's got the B building on it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And last question on this topic: When you say that the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina had that side, you're talking about the buildings with the F, the M, and the HI; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Let me try again. The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which side of the river did they have?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the right-hand side, downstream, on the right-hand side of the Miljacka river; not in the F and M buildings, but the first buildings next to Miljacka river, in Vilsonova Street. That's the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, I think we're miscommunicating. You're not saying that the army of the Republika Srpska controlled the Holiday Inn during the armed conflict, are you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What did you say? I did not understand the question. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I didn't understand your answer, so let's just take a minute and see if we can straighten this out. Look at the side of the river that has got the F building, the M building, and the HI building, and then answer this question: During the armed conflict, which army controlled the area with those buildings on it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army of Bosnia and Herzegovina had control of these buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I apologise for miscommunication.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: However, may I just answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Katic, with all respect, I think you have answered. I wonder if we could move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, let me hear the witness. What did you want to say, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, Presiding Judge. The troops of the BH army were not at the separation line located in those buildings: F, M, or HI. It was right next to the red line that I drew on the picture. The troops were on this side but not in the buildings, as I marked them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you would say that they still controlled those buildings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of this, all of this territory on the picture, was under the control of the BH army; however, the separation line is something different. It is as I indicated. The VRS was in the B building; and in the building to the left of B, which was Invest Bank, the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was along the red line. I even know which unit. It was King Tvrtko Battalion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think then I understand you to be saying that the army of the ABiH was physically located near to the line that you have indicated, but they controlled the entire area, including the areas in which we find the buildings marked F, M, and HI.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Well, let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, it is true, is it not, that the S-curve in the tram line that you testified about a few minutes ago is in front of the Holiday Inn, the building marked HI; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And it is true, is it not, that if there were snipers in the building marked B or in the building to its left, they could fire down that street, which we see going up and down in the photograph, towards the area of the S-curve, couldn't they?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if I may. May I? It was possible to shoot, if there were any snipers, from F to B as well; that is, it was possible to shoot from the red line at B.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. And you knew which unit of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was on the line in this position, and so I take it you also know that, other than those troops, there were no military targets down near the Holiday Inn, the faculty, or the museum; that is to say, no troop concentrations, no artillery, no ammunition depots, so forth and so on?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the side under the control of the BH army, around Holiday Inn or the Faculty of Philosophy?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm referring to a shot from the B building or the building to its left down the street into a tram on the S-curve.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You keep telling me that it was possible to shoot at a tram. To the right of Holiday Inn, although it's not shown in the photograph, there are buildings of the former Marshal Tito Barracks where members of the BH army were billeted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But we are going to stop now, because it's time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, just before the break, we were talking about the photograph that's on the screen in front of you, and I believe, at one point, you testified that it would be possible to shoot from the building marked F to the building marked B. Do you remember offering that observation?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Do you also remember testifying that there were no soldiers in the building marked F, that they were on the confrontation line marked by the red line along the Miljacka river?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that there were no troops on the building, either F or M building, but these buildings were under the control of the BH army; and at any time, depending on the need, soldiers could come and be deployed on F or M or HI building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You also, right before the break, when I asked about military targets in the area, mentioned the Marshal Tito Barracks. Do you remember giving that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, the Marshal Tito Barracks are out of the picture to the viewer's right; correct? In other words, you look at the picture and the Tito Barracks would be to your right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the right, below the Holiday Inn hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And I don't know the precise distance, but would you agree that the Marshal Tito Barracks would be several hundred metres away from what we are looking at in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Marshal Tito Barracks is below, to the right, of this photograph at a distance of about 500 metres; and, immediately, the beginning of the barracks, below Holiday Inn, is about 100 metres, perhaps even less.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Have you had opportunity, before coming here to testify, to look at the amended indictment in this case?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never seen the indictment, neither the original nor the amended one.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Would you have any reason to quarrel with me if I told you that the amended indictment alleges five specific instances of shooting, sniping trams in the area of the S-curve? You look puzzled. Do you need me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You say you have not read the amended indictment, and I'm asking you if you will accept that the amended indictment alleges five specific incidents of sniping on trams in front of the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Among other things, if that's one of the counts in the indictment, I haven't read it. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Okay. The reason I ask the question is this: If there were five trams shot at different times in front of the Holiday Inn, do I take it from your earlier answer that your view would be that that was all shooting at the Marshal Tito Barracks and missing and every time hitting a tram in the S-curve?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic has a point.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the witness is again asked to offer an opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. He's just asked to clarify the evidence that he has given; and he's specifically asked to say that when the indictment alleges that the tram was hit in the S-curve, is he saying that the intention was to hit the Marshal Tito Barracks and that the tram was mistakenly hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we are yet to establish how this happens and what witness knows about this. If the witness says that he said nothing about it, then I don't understand why the Prosecutor is asking this question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't understand the objection because the witness has given evidence, as I understand it, that the Marshal Tito Barracks is about 500 metres away from the area of the Holiday Inn, but that it begins just about 100 metres from the Holiday Inn. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour, Presiding Judge, that the barracks is about 100 metres from Holiday Inn, and it begins on the left -- on the right-hand side of this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you answer the question which counsel was asking you? Just repeat the question, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, right before the break, I asked you about the presence of military targets in the -- in the Holiday Inn area, and you offered in response the Marshal Tito Barracks. And as Mr. President has said, I'm trying to clarify that answer. If trams were hit by sniper fire in the S-curve, is it your evidence that this was the result of firing at the Tito Barracks but missing and hitting a tram by mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is precisely the problem. , Again, the question is "if" and/or "whether." The Court hasn't yet established whether the tram was hit at this location, and we are now, again, having a hypothesis put to the witness, and I think that this is not appropriate for cross-examination, although it can be wide. But in view of this hypothesis, I believe that this question is inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But has the witness not already testified about firing in that area? I believe he has. I consult my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber rules that in the context of the evidence that the witness has already given about firing in that area and snipers in that area and the positions of snipers, he should answer the question asked. Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Mr. President, Your Honour, Judge Robinson, never before during this testimony did the witness mention any knowledge about sniping, either coming from the VRS or the BH army. He never said that he knew anything about sniping. He even said -- he spoke about rifle shots, that's true; and if he is being asked about that, I have no objection. But he did not mention sniping once. He even said that he knew whether there was snipers on the side of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is a sufficient factual evidential basis for the question, and I have ruled that he is to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: After all that, do you remember the question, or shall I ask it again?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the question. You don't need to put it to me again. I will try to give you an answer. I said where the barracks was. You claim that a tram was hit, but what I can say is that at the moment there could have been, in front of Holiday Inn, a moveable vehicle with a mortar mounted on it or a machine-gun. It was possible from the building B, or from the building to the left of building B, to observe a military target and between the buildings F and M.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Last question on this point, and then we'll move on. From that last answer, which now gets into mobile mortars rather than the Marshal Tito Barracks, are you still asserting that the Marshal Tito Barracks -- that missing the Marshal Tito Barracks was a reason for hitting a tram, or are you withdrawing that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, he hasn't asserted that, as far as I know. I believe you are trying to elicit that from him, but he hasn't really said so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In any event, let me withdraw that question. Mr. Katic, whether shooting at the Marshal Tito Barracks and missing -- excuse me. Whether shooting at the Marshal Tito Barracks and missing or whether this mobile mortar that you talk about was shuttling around in the area south-west, somebody was shooting at it; correct? And as you said, I believe, the building marked B offers a good vantage point on to it, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but also from the F and the M in the opposite direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And are you aware that UNPROFOR troops were frequently stationed at the intersection of that street that runs up and down in the photograph and the street that runs left and right in the photograph, and are you aware that there are no UNPROFOR documents indicating the -- indicating a mobile mortar operating in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know about the UNPROFOR presence in this area was something that I learned from the media. I used to watch evening news and I saw what was happening in the territory of the city of Sarajevo, but I didn't go over there to see where they were precisely positioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you ever see a mobile mortar in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did you ever talk to anyone who saw a mobile mortar in that area or see an official report of a mobile mortar in that area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I talked to the people who had left Sarajevo following the conflict, or rather, the end of the war, or who had left across the Brotherhood and Unity bridge. They used to tell me about these mobile vehicles with weapons mounted on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Did they tell you that these mobile vehicles with weapons mounted on them had been operating in this area, in the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They didn't mention specific locations, but, rather, the territory of Sarajevo under the control of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina; therefore, I am not able to say that these people talked to me specifically about this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Could I tendered this photograph, please, Mr. President, but could it remain on the screen for a few more minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As P754, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, maybe it would help if we talked about a specific case. Are you aware of a shooting of a mother and child at the intersection of those two streets on 18th November 1994. The mother was named Dzenana Sokolovic; the boy was Nermin Divovic.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, and I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Then we'll move on. You testified, in your evidence in-chief, that although had you seen men with rifles in Grbavica going in and out of the buildings, they did not have telescopic sights; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I'm going to put to you something that was in the Judgement in the case of Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic, and it's found at paragraph 238, page 86 of the English version of the Trial Chamber's Judgement. And it's concerning the testimony of a man named Van Lynden, Aernout Van Lynden, who is a Dutch English journalist. "Van Lynden recounted that in late November 1993 the Bosnian Serb Presidency permitted him to visit apartment blocks in Grbavica, close to the Miljacka river, where he observed front line sniping positions. He was taken to rooms" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Tapuskovic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Van Lynden was supposed to come as a witness for the Prosecution here, but he didn't appear. I believe that this witness cannot be put with something that relates to a different case, because no cross-examination of Van Lynden was possible here in order for to us check. We had some serious questions for Witness Van Lynden. He is mentioned very often in this judgement, and we have proof but I'm not going to discuss this. He hasn't been examined or cross-examined here and, therefore, I believe that this putting statements from a different case is inadmissible to the witness, which relates to the witness that was not examined in the course of the proceedings. This is my general objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: My initial response is the same as the one I gave when you jumped up prematurely. I'd like to hear the question before I make a ruling. So I'd like counsel to conclude the citation; and then when we hear the question which he has asked, we'll consider it. We'll consider the objection that you have made.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Just going on with the quotation from paragraph 238: "He described the rifles as being long barrelled and as having telescopic sights." Does that cause you to rethink your earlier answer about the presence of sniper rifles with telescopic sights in the high-rise buildings in Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What period did that evidence cover, Mr. Docherty?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: The visit was late September 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And what period are you questioning the witness in relation to?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Initially, that same period. Obviously, I have some follow-on questions, but they don't concern Mr. Van Lynden. But this is a witness who has testified about the entirety of the armed conflict, including even events that occurred in Sarajevo before the outbreak of the armed conflict, which was his testimony concerning the events in the park in Vrace.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The Chamber sees no objection to the witness being asked the question posed by counsel, which is whether the passage that he has cited would cause him to rethink his earlier answer about the presence of sniper rifles with telescopic sights in the high-rise buildings in Grbavica. What you have heard Counsel just quote, would that cause you to change your view, Witness? Simply, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to give an answer. Since the question was put it me whether, in 1992, in September of that year, there were snipers in high-rise buildings in Grbavica, my answer is I don't know, because at the time I didn't go to separation lines at Grbavica and observe the troops in that period. I was at the line which I described in my previous evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's discuss some evidence that does concern the time that you were back as the president of the assembly of Srpsko Novo Sarajevo. So I will move away from September 1992 and I will go back to the 18 the of November, 1994, and I understand you have no person knowledge of the alleged sniping on that date. However, I do want to draw your attention to some testimony from someone who was here earlier in this trial, a man named John Jordan, a former American marine, who was the leader of a group of fire-fighters in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And for the record, Mr. President, I'm going to be citing to transcript page 2651 of this trial, line 11, through 2652, line 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And Mr. Jordan was asked why he had positioned a fire truck in a particular position on the street that we see running up and down in this photograph and gave the following answer: "The vehicle is between the child and the man who killed him, straight down that street to the high buildings controlled by the Bosnian Serb army." My question, Mr. Katic, is: There were, in fact, I put it to you, snipers, in the building marked B and in the building immediately to its left, who fired upon the Marindvor area and specifically on civilians in the Marindvor area?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are claiming that those were snipers. I'm claiming that there was shooting, but I don't know whether it was a sniper fire, and I assert that these were not snipers. Whether they had hit this child and this lady, I know nothing about this incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: I understand you know nothing about the incident. But if the claim has are narrowed to one that there was shooting but not sniping, then let's talk about some evidence of sniping versus shooting?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, I need now to discuss the testimony of a protected witness. Can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, let's try and clarify where we agree and where we disagree. I think we both agree that there were soldiers with rifles on the VRS side of the Miljacka river; correct? I don't think there is any controversy about that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: You seem to be putting a lot of weight on the distinction between shooting and sniping. When one shoots at something, one levels the gun, sights at the target, and squeezes the trigger; correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Is only difference, in your mind, the presence or absence of the telescopic sight, or is there more to it than that, this distinction you seem to be making between shooting on the one hand and sniping on the other hand?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you put a telescopic sight on a semi-automatic or automatic rifle, then you have a sniper. That's a what it is called. Without the telescopic sights, and with it, the semi-automatic rifle or automatic rifle actually function in the same way. You open fire in the same way. The only reason why you put the telescopic sights is to be able to see the target better. I don't know if we can agree on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: So just to make clear, I think the differences between us have significantly narrowed. You are saying that sniping requires as telescopic sight and that did you not see men with telescopic sight. Is that as far as you're willing to go?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There were, though, men with guns, rifles, on the upper floors on the building marked with the B and the building to its left that's on the photograph in front of us, weren't there, Maybe without telescopic sights, but there were men with rifles up there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And from those positions, could shoot down, I'll say, the natural funnel formed by that up-and-down street to hit targets in front of the Holiday Inn, if they chose to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Now, there was --

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I have just one moment? I just need to consult about something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: There was a Pakistani officer, who had served with UNPROFOR, who testified here, named Muhamed Butt; and in his testimony, he stated that a human being could be effectively engaged from those buildings on the VRS side of the river to Marindvor with or without a telescopic sight. Do you accept or reject his testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: And then last question on this topic, and then we'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: "Yes," meaning what? "Yes," meaning that he accepts that a human being could be effectively engaged from the VRS side of the river with our without a telescopic sight. Are you agreeing with that proposition.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this picture, where this is red letter D, it looks like a red letter D. It's not a marking; it just looks like a red letter D. I don't know if you can see it. That's the famous red building. It is divided between the Republika Srpska army and Bosnia-Herzegovina army. One doorway was held by one side; the other was held by the other. And, now, in order to provoke or to cause incidents, it was possible to open fire from that building, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes. We hear that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour, but I do want to state that because of these incidents, in order to cause such incidents, the BH army soldiers stationed at the famous red building - that's what it was called in the media and was known throughout the world - they could have opened fire on this location with this purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So you're saying passengers on a tram, in the S area opposite the Holiday Inn, could be just as easily as readily targeted by soldiers on the red building, which includes soldiers of the ABiH who held one side, as they could be targeted by soldiers from the B building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. President, with the Court's leave, that last answer of the witness, I do not believe could possibly have been predicted from his 65 ter summary, which says nothing concerning the red building or this sort of activity; and with the Court's leave, as the Court knows, when we were introducing evidence from crime base witnesses, on the various, video we had a 360 degree view from ground level of the area where person was shot. And I want to show one of those to the witness now because I believe that it will show the buildings with the B and the one to the left are there and the red building is not. However, that was on the -- this sheet that we sent to the Defence, but I think the reasons are understandable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tapuskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that there is no witness that -- that we proposed to talk about the fighting at the separation line. There's -- I can't see why Mr. Docherty now says that we did not include this in his summary. He spoke about the separation lines at the time when he was serving as a soldier and later on in his examination-in-chief. So this is what we stated in the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you objecting to what Mr. Docherty is now proposing to do, to show the witness this map which does not have the red building. Is that what you're proposing to do, Mr. Docherty.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let me hear from Mr. Docherty exactly what he is proposing to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm proposing to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So I'm asking, are you objecting to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TAPUSKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I'm merely stating for the record that the witness was supposed to talk about those topics. That's why we called him, but we are not opposed to the Prosecutor using this. But what Mr. Docherty had said is not really appropriate, because he alleged that we did not bring this witness in order to testify about combat activities. This is precisely what he was supposed to be testifying about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm getting a bit confused and would like to put a question just for clarification. I believe that the issue is whether it is possible to hit a target in the S-curve in front of the Holiday Inn from any position in the ready building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And that the Prosecution now intends to show the 360-degrees photo circle that was taken from the crossing, in order to prove or to establish that from that point you cannot see the ready building. The only buildings can you see from the crossing is the Metalka building and the bank building. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: In effect, yes, Judge Harhoff. I also think that this photograph, which is on the screen, I for one would have a very difficult time visualizing a shot through all of those buildings along the river, into the are of the S curve.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But, still, since we do not know the elevation on the ground on the south side of the river, it could be possible. So by showing your 360-degree line of photos, we might be able to see whether or not from the crossing it is possible to see the red building.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: That's why I would like to show it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's get on with it then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Bosnjakovic, could you please call up the 360 for scheduled sniping incident number 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
utterances.text: Mr. Katic, do you see the still photograph that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD KATIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOCHERTY
